articleTitle: A Novel Sub-Multilevel Cell (SMC) with Increased Ratio of Number of Levels to Number of Sources and Switches
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, a new 31-level Developed H-Bridge based Sub-Multilevel Cell (DHBSMC) is proposed that can be extended to create more steps. The suggested configuration has large number of steps per device count. The suggested DHBSMC has simple structure and can be well applied for any load type (resistive, inductive or resistive-inductive). The amplitude of DC supplies can be chosen freely. In this paper, 3 methodologies are suggested for deciding about amplitude of power supplies. The generalized multi-level topology, which is the expanded version of suggested DHBSMC, is introduced. The suggested DHBSMC is contrasted with similar topologies and simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC. The results verify appropriate performance of suggested configuration.

articleTitle: A Proposed Configuration Based on Three-Level Boost Converter for Unbalancing Voltage issue in Photovoltaic Systems Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In photovoltaic systems, there are problems such as shading and dust, which causes a difference in the electrical power production of each panel. A practical solution to this issue is distributed maximum power point tracking, in which separate converters used for each panel. However, using this method increases the stress on the circuit elements, the possibility of a loss of controllability and increasing the error of the maximum power point tracking algorithm due to the voltage unbalancing issue that is created in this method. This paper tries to solve the unbalancing voltage issue by proposing a new configuration of converters. This new configuration includes two three-level boost converters, which one of their capacitors is shared. For controlling of the proposed two modules three-level converter, the sliding mode controller is used, and the simulation results of the system are presented.

articleTitle: A Modified Single-Phase Multi-Level Inverter with Increased Number of Steps
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, a modified single-phase Multi-Level Inverter (MLI) is proposed that produces more steps per device count, which reduces less total expense, volume, weight and losses. The low Normalized Blocking Voltage (NBV) on switches is another advantage that results in reduced expense, volume and losses of switches and consequently higher efficiencies. Due to increased steps, the suggested configuration has low Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and consequently high power quality. The proposed 49-level topology has been introduced, explained and compared with recently presented novel MLIs. For performance verification, the PSCAD/EMTDC has been used as simulation software. Comparison and simulation results approve the suitability of suggested configuration.

articleTitle: A New Cascaded 35-Level Inverter with Reduced Switch Count
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a new topology for cascaded 35-level inverters. Higher number of produced levels (35 levels in this paper) improves the quality of output voltage and reduces its Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). For producing 35 levels, the suggested configuration employs less switches than similar structures. This means that the share of each switch in suggested configuration on generating voltage steps is more than that of similar structures. Reduction in switch count leads to reduced driver circuits and finally reduces the complexity, volume, weight and expense of suggested configuration. The fundamental frequency strategy has been applied for switching of proposed topology. The suggested configuration can be employed on supplying low/medium power factor (R-L) loads. The simulation results approve correct operation of suggested configuration.

articleTitle: Wind and Solar Farms Site Selection Using Geographical Information System (GIS), Based on Multi Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) Methods: A Case-Study for East-Azerbaijan
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Economic and industrial development raise the demand for energy. Renewable energies have replaced fossil fuels. because the fossil fuels emission greenhouse gases and damage the environment. The sitting of renewable power plants is of great importance because there is a direct relationship between the production efficiency and the location of the renewable power plant. In this paper, using of multi criteria decision making (MCDM) methods a suitable location for the construction of a renewable power plant is proposed. Prioritization map of the hybrid power plant was prepared using AHP, VICORE and TOPSIS. The final map is obtained of the overlap of other maps.

Author Keywords: Echnique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS)

articleTitle: A New Multi-Phase High Step-Up DC-DC Converter Appropriate for PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper suggests a new multi-phase dc-dc converter that benefits from modularity, simple control and structure, extra gain, continuous input current and low normalized voltage stress on switches/diodes. The suggested configuration can track the maximum power point in PV applications. The suggested configuration produces larger gains per device count, in comparison with other topologies. After introduction of suggested configuration, its operational modes have been explained. Then, its effectiveness has been verified by comparison and simulation results.

articleTitle: A Novel Control Strategy for On-Grid Photovoltaic Systems Based on Adaptive PI Control
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel control strategy for grid-connected photovoltaic system based on adaptive PI. The proposed control strategy has following steps: implementation of beta algorithm for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in photovoltaic system; dc link voltage stabilization; and grid current control utilizing model reference adaptive control (MRAC-PI) method. In the proposed control method, the coefficients of PI are continuously estimated based on MIT rule in order to decrease error between reference values and controlling variables. Simulation results of the proposed controller confirm the robust performance in uncertainty of irradiance. Comparing with optimized classic PI controllers, utilizing PSO algorithm, proposed controller has a better performance in the both transient and steady state conditions.

articleTitle: Commandability of a modular Three-Level Boost Converter in Fuel-cell Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In Fuel-cell systems, there are problems such as flooding and aging, which cause low output power. Separating one huge stack into several small stacks might lead to a better solution, which can extract the maximum power from each stack, and this method makes higher overall efficiency. Each small stack is connected to a DC-DC switching converter. In this paper, two input three-level boost converter is presented. The command zones of this converter are investigated. The input powers corresponding to the possible duty cycle commands are studied. The simulation results corresponding to the theoretical analysis are given to validate the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Locating Renewable Energy Generators Using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, renewable energies have replaced fossil fuels. In renewable energies, there is a dependency between energy efficiency and costs with the power plants location. because of this sitting of power plants is very important. This paper presents a framework for creating a model using the KNN algorithm to select a suitable location for construction wind and solar power plants.

articleTitle: A Novel Extra High Gain Non-Isolated DC-DC Converter With Continuous Input/Output Current
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper suggests a novel dc-dc topology that produces extra high gains in mild duty cycles. The main profits of suggested topology are: simple control and structure, continuous input/output currents and low standing voltage of power switches/diodes. In this paper, the new structure is introduced and its operating principles and analysis are given. Then, the suggested configuration is compared with similar novel structures. Also, the proposed topology has been simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC software. The presented comparison and simulation results verify satisfactory operation of suggested converter.

articleTitle: A New Decentralized Control Strategy for Hybrid Energy Storage System in Islanded DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Today, the use of DC power equipments is increasing due to the cost-effective use of energy and decreasing power losses in the conversions. Generally in microgrids the hybrid energy storage system (HESS) composed of battery and supercapacitor (SC) is used to improve the microgrid reliability and increase battery and supercapacitor lifetime. Maintaining the SOC of battery and supercapacitor in permissible range is an important task to offset the uncertainty of renewable energy sources. Therefore, the energy management system plays an important role in continuous and reliable operation of the microgrid. In this paper, a DC microgrid including photovoltaic cells, battery and supercapacitor with the proposed control system is modeled and simulated. The purpose of the proposed control system is performance improvement of supercapacitors and their proper operation during step load changes. In the proposed supercapacitor control system, the double loop voltage-current controller with virtual impedance loop is used, which makes the supercapacitor current become zero during steady state of the system and produces a surge current during step load changes. The purpose of the proposed control scheme is to increase the efficiency of HESS specially SC in the case of step load change and voltage transients in the islanded DC microgrid system. The proposed control system is simulated by Matlab/Simulink and its effectiveness is evaluated under different scenarios and the results are analyzed.

articleTitle: Design of the hybrid harmonic filter to improve power quality of the grid connected hybrid renewable energy system
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With advancement of technology, renewable energy sources have become more economical, and network loads have become more sensitive to power quality. Renewable Energy systems due to the voltage converters used in their structure, cause power quality problems such as harmonic distortion in the power grid. And also increasing the penetration of Renewable Energy Sources can increase power quality problems. In this paper to improve power quality of the renewable energy system, a parallel hybrid harmonic filter is proposed. The hybrid harmonic filter is a combination of active and passive filter that work together to compensate harmonics in the renewable energy system. In the hybrid filter, size and number of passive filters, hysteresis bandwidth and PI controller gains of the active filter, are optimized by NSGA-II Algorithm. The results show performance of the proposed hybrid harmonic filter.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of Electric Vehicle Parking Lots to Improve Self-healing Property of Smart Grid in Islanding Mode
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Self-healing is one of the power system's strategies for increasing system reliability under the emergency. Self-healing property first detects the location of the fault and then by grid reconfiguration and servicing to the loads maintains the adequacy of the system. Planning the charging and discharging of electric vehicles, as well as the optimal allocation of parking lots as a distributed energy resources in order to inject electric power into the smart grid during the fault, creates the potential that can simultaneously maintain the network parameters at the optimal level and has the least load shedding. Because the islanding mode is one of the common modes of network fault, in this research the optimal allocation of parking lots has been studied to improve the self-healing property of the smart grid in islanding mode. The studied system is the 12-bus network of the Ulleungdo Island in South Korea. In this paper, firstly using the HOMER software, the power of electrical resources is calculated at the desired geographic location under normal conditions. Secondly, the system is modeled after the fault by General Algebraic Modeling System (GAMS) software, and the optimal location and size of the parking lots and the amount of curtailment of the distributed generation sources are determined by Synchronous Branch and Bound (SBB) algorithm. The objective functions of the problem include the reducing of power losses and demand-not-supplied, and improving the voltage quality. The results of the simulation indicate the high efficiency of the proposed method for reducing the load shedding.

Author Keywords: Plug –in hybrid electric vehicle parking lots

articleTitle: Rrefuse-derived Fuels (RDF) Analysis for Energy Generation and its usage in various Sectors
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Nowadays, environmental pollution, energy deficiency and an increasing need for energy as well as insufficient land are considered as the main global issues. Due to exponential growth of earth' population, urbanization and consumerism, one of the main environmental contaminants and land occupational factor is municipal solid waste (MSW), which deteriorates gradually owing to old methods like burying or waste disposal in landfills.On the other hand, it is more likely to generate clean and renewable energy by MSW processing and transfer them into refuse-derived fuels (RDF) with high thermal quality and value. RDF is a non-hazardous fuel with closed carbon cycle which can be used to meet the energy requirements in industries and different types of power plants. In the current research, however, the main purpose is to study and analyze various techniques of RDF production and consumption, to explain RDF usage in cement industry, power plants and energy extraction technologies, and in the end, to illustrate the effects and consequences of replacing harmful fossil fuels such as coal with RDF.

articleTitle: Retail Electricity Pricing Impacts on Demand Response and Electrical Vehicles Planning in Residential Micro-grid
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, proposing the novel solutions to boost the efficiency of power systems and optimal management of energy consumption has become increasingly significant. Demand response (DR) program as an essential part of Demand-side-management (DSM), has always been one of the most efficient ways to attract consumers to alter their power consumption patterns. In general, DR’s programs can be carried out by implementing electricity retail pricing. In this paper, first, an overview of the principles and rules of retail electricity pricing in the context of Smart Grid is presented. Then, new retail pricing methods have been applied in an optimization framework of energy management in Micro-grid. It can be noted that the analysis of this residential Micro-grid is performed with the presence of multi-carrier energy including electricity and gas systems. Also, a hybrid tariff plan, that is more in line with other pricing principles is proposed to evaluate its effectiveness in studied home micro-grid surveyed. To appraise the efficiency of the optimization framework and the proposed method of retail electricity pricing, numerous numerical studies have been done. Finally, simulation results indicate that the economic and social indicators including benefit, energy payment cost (EPC) and social welfare of the customer are optimized by zeroing out EPC and receiving a daily charge of about 1.31 pounds –on average- due to the presence in the retail electricity market.

articleTitle: A New Step-Up Four-Switch Resonant LCC DC/DC Converter for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Resonant power conversion is an efficient solution for transmitting power from renewable energy resources to loads. Step-up DC/DC converters have been widely used in photovoltaic (PV) applications for increasing the voltage of PV arrays to a standard value. This paper proposes a new fourswitch resonant converter that includes a neutral point clamped topology, a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order resonant tank (LCC), a high-frequency transformer and a fast bridge rectifier. The proposed topology is controlled by a self-oscillating resonant controller that guarantees the zero current switching (ZCS) and zero voltage switching (ZVS) in this topology. Simulation results have been done for a 72V/300V/900W prototype. Results validate the proposed topology and its control unit.

articleTitle: Analysis of DFIG During Unsymmetrical Grid Fault by Using Crowbar Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Throughout the last decade, the number of wind installations have increased greatly. One of them which has the most portion in penetration of wind turbines, is doubly fed induction generator (DFIG). Notwithstanding this variable speed machine's benefits, there are some inherent drawbacks. One of the most important concerns is to provide Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT) capability during different grid faults. In this paper, some solutions on this issue have been reviewed and a method is proposed to avoid the weaknesses of the other solutions. in order to compare these methods, a 9MW wind farm which consists of 6 DFIGs, connected to a grid, is studied in its normal condition and during an asymmetrical fault. The simulation results are attained by using MATLAB/ Simulink.

articleTitle: Maximum power extraction for switched reluctance generator wind turbine using optimal firing angles control
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This article is study of firing angles control for switched reluctance generator (SRG) in order to maximize wind power extraction and also efficiency of generator. In the proposed method, optimum turn-on and turn-off angles in offline mode were attained based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to control the system online with linear interpolation. The main features of the present scenario include simple structure, low executing time, and reasonable convergence rate which is independent from machine characteristics (regardless to the highly nonlinear behavior of SRG) and simultaneously investigates the firing angles. In order to consider more realistic conditions, copper losses, switching and conduction losses of semiconductors were included in the simulations. Ultimately, Matlab was used to perform the proposed method on typical three-phase 6/4 generator and the results confirm the validation of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Model Based on Neural networks to Predict the Power Output of Photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, solar power has been a major contributor to the global network. However, due to the nature of the periodicity of this energy, its integration with the network has challenges and problems that simultaneously predict the exact output power of photovoltaic systems (pv) is very important. In this article, a hybrid model consisting of kohonen Self-organizing Map (SOM), Feedforward Neural Network (FFNN), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithms are proposed for prediction of pv power output. In fact, in this model, using the SOM and KNN algorithms, the data of weather input is classified and then by FFNN, a prediction model for each class is presented. The results confirm the high accuracy of the proposed model in the prediction.

articleTitle: Maximum power point tracking in small wind turbine with permanent magnet generator using voltage sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In wind turbine technologies, the type of control system is determined by the turbine size, system's sensitivity, and their cost. In the case of small wind turbines, due to the cost and structure of the turbine, a simple, low-cost control system with good performance is required. A permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) is used to extract electrical power. The power of the small wind energy converter system (SWECS) is controlled using only one voltage sensor. In this method, the proposed controller has been tested in urban variable winds. The results are compared with the Perturb and Observe (P&O) method. Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) simulation has been tested in the Matlab / Simulink. The results show that this method has quick Response and accuracy for wind turbine control in urban wind conditions. On the other hand, using the proposed method will cause a reduction in the cost of construction and maintenance and it brings the simplicity of implementation.

articleTitle: New Control Strategy for Optimum use of Regenerative Braking Energy in Electric Train based on Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: A novel energy management strategy based on the energy storage system in series with DC side of electric train inverter is proposed in this paper. Using the energy storage system causes the increase of the right side voltage of electric train inverter, consequently, the motor torque is improved as the train brakes at high speeds. Also, this control strategy increases motor acceleration during the normal operation. In this method, the electric double layer capacitor instead of the battery is used to increase the voltage because of its fast dynamic cycles and higher power density. In addition, the residual energy of braking in the normal operation mode is also used by other trains. In this case, field oriented control (FOC) strategy is used to traction motors control. By employing the proposed method, the braking energy that has a high amount in the metropolitans can be used effectively. The simulations are done by the MATLAB/Simulink<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">@</sup>. The results validate the effectiveness of this control strategy.

articleTitle: Effect of Cleaning, Cooling and Shading on Current and Electrical Power of Photovoltaic Panels
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to determine the effect of cleaning, cooling and shading on the current and electrical power produced by photovoltaic panels. A practical experiment at the solar site of the Renewable Energy Laboratory of Shahid Beheshti University was arranged on a part of the panels installed at the pilot plant of the laboratory. The results are presented and discussed in this paper. For this purpose, an overview of previous work and articles published in this field is first provided, and then the results of this field experiment are presented. The analysis of the data obtained from this experiment shows that the removal of dust from the surface of the photovoltaic panels and the cooling of the panels, increases the electrical power generated by these panels by approximately 10%. Also, the result of this test shows, the half shadowing may cause to completely cut-off the electrical current output of photovoltaic panels. Due to the fact that Iran is located in the desert belt of the planet, most cities of Iran in most seasons of the year witness winds with dust, which reduces the electrical power production and efficiency of the installed photovoltaic panels. Therefore, the results of this experiment can be used to improve the performance of photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: PR-Fuzzy Control Improvement of Doubly Fed Induction Generator During Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: By increasing the penetration of wind energy, it is necessary to study the behavior of different wind generators in different types of grid condition. One of the most important types of wind generators is a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG). However, these generators also have problems during the power grid faults, which should be taken into account. Usually, these generators are controlled in a system that has a proportional integral controller. but proportional resonant controller (PR) has some advantages in comparison with PI controller. so, in this paper, an improved control strategy for rotor and grid side converter is presented based on the PR controller tuned to the grid frequency. On the other hand, DFIG is used in a dynamic system. so proportional and resonant gains must be adapted to the requirements of the system. Fuzzy controllers that designs based on information taken from system behavior can continuously adjust the control system parameters so that system performance improves. Therefore, in this paper, proportional resonant controllers tuned with fuzzy system are used to control the rotor and grid converter. The simulation result shows the improvement of generator performance during grid faults in comparison with control methods based on conventional strategies.

articleTitle: Effect of solidity on the performance of micro-scale darrieus wind turbines: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Recently micro scale wind turbines have received special attention in particular in urban industry. One of the influential parameters of these turbines is the rotor solidity coefficient. In this research, the effect of solidity change, defined based on the chord length of the blade, on the performance of micro darrieus vertical axis wind turbines (VAWT) with straight blades is experimentally studied. For this purpose, three different rotors with different solidities are designed and constructed. The power output of the turbines is measured with respect to different tip speed ratios (TSR). The reults show that the best performance of the turbines occur at the solidity value which is higher compared to the values presented by previous investigations as the optimum one.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Behavior of the Grid-Connected Flywheel in Presence of Different Faults
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Uncertainty of electricity generation is a big issue of renewable distributed generation units. One of the efficient solutions is using energy storage (ES) systems to damp any under/over shoots in energy flow in the micro grids. Another application of ES is improvement of power quality in the network in conditions such as voltage sags. In this paper, the behavior of a Flywheel energy storage system is analyzed considering different fault types. Because of high inertia constant of the mechanical part of Flywheel, the reaction of this equipment is different from other equipment in the network. So it is important to study any malfunction of the flywheels to avoid damages to flywheel and also other parts of the network. All important types of faults are applied to the point of common coupling (PCC). The time domain simulation package is employed for better analysis and results are presented in detail.

articleTitle: Multi-Variable PI Control Design for Grid-Tied Three-Phase PV Inverters
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The grid-tied inverter modeling and control are among the most important issues in efficient utilization of the renewable energy sources connected to the grid. In this paper, the three-phase grid-tied inverter as a Multi-Input Multi-Output (MI-MO) system is considered for which a PI control system is designed using multi-variable control systems analysis and design techniques. Similar PI controllers are employed for the plant's input channels in the synchronous reference frame. The inverter's dead-time and un-balanced grid conditions are considered as disturbances in this study. The performance of designed closed-loop control system is evaluated for different conditions by simulations in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Power Generation Using Trains
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Wind energy is one of the most renewable sources that has a very high potential for use. This paper presents a method for producing electric energy using the kinetic energy of wind by installing special wind turbines in locomotives. Many studies have been conducted on the installation of wind turbines near the railway (tunnels, large fields, etc.), but few of these papers focus on wind turbines as part of their locomotives and trains. Wind energy causes the wind turbine to travel through the train movement. Several designs have been taken so far on the installation of wind turbines along the train rails. The movement of the train itself would cause the wind to flow through the wind turbine blades mounted on the locomotive. In this paper, two types of known wind turbines are studied and then a complementary method and complement is proposed in Siemens ER24PC locomotive engines used in Iranian railway systems. Reducing the fuel consumption of trains is carefully considered based on the generated power. A battery storage system is also proposed that provides power over low wind speeds.

articleTitle: Fatigue Sensitivity Analysis to Piles Fixity length in Offshore Wind Turbines Jacket Substructures
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Fatigue damage has always been a significant concern for engineers regarding offshore structures applications. This phenomenon is investigated, especially for lattice structures such as jackets in which tubular welded connections are the most critical points threatened with fatigue failure. Fatigue damage, moreover, for jacket-type offshore wind turbines have relatively been examined in literature focusing on structural considerations. However, since most offshore wind turbines simulation programmes use simplified soil-pile interaction models such as Apparent Fixity model; fatigue analyses concerning such models, especially the Apparent Fixity model, have not been investigated so far. More specifically, the impacts of different apparent fixity lengths on fatigue damage in jacket-type offshore wind turbines have not been taken into account. In this study, fatigue analysis of the jacket-type offshore wind turbine supported by "Upwind" reference jacket for different pile fixity lengths is carried out considering both wave and wind loads applied on the structure. Apparent fixity model is used herein for soil-pile interaction. Ultimately, a sensitivity analysis for fatigue damage to different pile fixity lengths is carried out in order to find how accumulated fatigue damage is changed. It is concluded that fatigue life of a connection -the most vulnerable one to fatigue damage - in jacket substructures of the offshore wind turbines is considerably sensitive to pile fixity length when applying Apparent Fixity model for soil-pile interaction.

articleTitle: Decentralized Adaptive Protection Structure for Microgrids Based on Multi–Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive protection structure based on multi - agent systems is presented. Short circuit currents in microgrids (MGs) are dependent on the uncertainty of distributed generation sources especially renewable sources and operation modes (connected or islanded mode). There are many challenges in MG protection studies considering the issues. It is impossible to use the conventional relays in MG structure due to that the short circuit current is directly depend on MG. In this study, an adaptive smart relay based on multi-agent systems is introduced which, based on received data from other factors, detect MG topology smartly and update settings and coordination issues of the relay according to the MG topology. Fast operation and high reliability are the main advantages of the proposed protection system structure.

articleTitle: The Role of Predictive Maintenance in the Continuity of the Food Enegy Water Nexus; A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The concept that Food, Energy and Water (FEW) systems are interdependent-not easily disentangled- is now part of modern development. One of the most important items in FEW systems is continuous production while the economic targets are satisfied as well as end-user needs. In this paper, a new concept will be discussed to prevent interrupts in the food production called predictive maintenance. Predictive maintenance allows to employee different modern techniques for mining big data and recognizing accurate patterns as much as possible. Therefore it's possible to predict system failure before it occurs and mitigate interrupts. As an example of FEW system, some food processing and packaging factories that are supported by predictive maintenance are analyzed and finally results are compared with past production performances.

articleTitle: Energy Management System for Isolated Microgrids: A Coordinated UC-OPF-Based Stochastic Programming
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel mathematical approach for modelling microgrids' Energy Management System (EMS), administrating distributed energy resources, such as diesel gensets, wind turbines, photovoltaic units, and energy storage systems, optimally and reliably. In the proposed approach, the EMS is designed based on a coordinated Unit Commitment-Optimal Power Flow (UC-OPF) framework, yielding optimal power dispatch decisions for gensets and storage units. In this approach, the UC operational constraints, such as ramp characteristics and minimum up and down times of gensets are considered while the power flow equations are taken into account, simultaneously. Being a severe source of uncertainty, the wind power generation deviation is handled using scenario-based stochastic programming technique. In order to evaluate the proposed system, a complex microgrid based on a CIGRE benchmark is used. The results indicate that the EMS optimal dispatch decisions are highly influenced by the uncertainty of wind generation compared to the deterministic assumptions made for this source of generation.

articleTitle: p10 MW on Grid Solar Power Plant Performance Due to Temperature Changes
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The operation of solar cells declines with increasing temperature. Temperature plays a significant role in the efficiency of solar power plants and the output power of them. So that the amount of produced power in the warm seasons is significantly reduced. In this paper, the performance of the 10 MW solar power plant located in Zahedan, Iran (SAMA solar power plant) has been investigated in different days and the effects of temperature on the production power, and total efficiency of the power plant have been studied. The consequences illustrate that the performance of the solar power plant has significantly decreased in the warm summer days.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Feasibility Analysis of a Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Power Plant in Shahid Beheshti University, Iran
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Today, grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) power plants become widely used and fast growing around the world. In this regard, Iran has an appropriate location in terms of solar irradiation and other meteorological parameters that make it attractive to investing for solar power plants. Although these plants currently have a high initial cost, but the low maintenance and the support mechanisms that governments have established to guaranteed purchase power from these power plants, usually by means of defining feed-in-tariff especially in Iran, has led to investing in this field Be very attractive. In this paper, a feasibility study was conducted for a solar power plant at Shahid beheshti University. At first, the site is analyzed in terms of climate, then it is technically reviewed and pre-designed and the results of the software will be presented. Eventually, an economic feasibility study will also be done for the desired location.

articleTitle: Novel sliding mode controller for power control of a doubly fed induction generator in variable speed wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this study, two sliding mode controllers (SMCs) are proposed for active power control and maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) in a variable speed wind turbine. The parametric indeterminacy and uncertainty results in inaccurate performance of the DFIG-wind turbine system and may lead to instability. The proposed SMCs can properly overcome the problems caused by parametric indeterminacy and rejects the disturbances. A new proportional-integral-type SMC (PI- SMC) is proposed by using control Lyapunov function method, also a new second-order SMC (SO-SMC) is designed by using the super-twisting algorithm. The proposed PI-SMC and SO- SMC are applied to the rotor side convertor (RSC) of DFIG in order to reduce the negative impact of chattering phenomena and increase the tracking accuracy. The simulation results of the proposed methods and vector control optimized by dragonfly algorithm, are compared, Wich results prove that using the SMCs leads to lower ripple and higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Environmental impacts of industrial sweetener with CHP and desalination and its disadvantages in the Persian Gulf ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Nowadays there are various techniques for desalination. Some pass waters with high pressure through microscopic membranes, so microscopic that even viruses cannot pass through its holes, Salt molecules are separated from water and the result is sweet water (the amount of sweetening depends on our choice). In another type of desalination, saltwater is evaporated and then it cools again, so sweat water remains. It is exactly the thing which distillation devices do. It is not important what and how these devices operate. What matters is the thing remains of these devices. Sweet water is the most important part remains; this is the philosophy of the existence of these devices. Except for sweet water, bitter water is abided too. The bitter water is hot, distasteful and bad scenery. This water is much warmer than normal seawater and its other salts (such as salt and other minerals) are higher than the salinity of the sea. So what should we do with this bitter water. The simplest answer is to find a way to its source or sea. Usually, desalination is placed near the sea. They receive water with pressure and soften the water there, then they give it back to the sea. In this process, many samples of environmental degradation occur which we cannot escape with the available level of technology. The desalination is forced to squeeze the water into their inner layers. Many microscopic organisms in the seas (such as planktons) and even small crustaceans or tiny fish cannot withstand this extreme pressure and water poisoning, and they cannot resist then they go to desalination and disappear. Once this becomes more serious, we know that most of these microscopic beings are the beginning of the sea's life chain, and without them, aquatic life is in danger of being completely destroyed.

articleTitle: Provides a new method for detecting and retrieving small scale generators
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Electricity demand has increased pressure on extension of generation and distribution capacity, all around the world. This is an undesirable stage in modern restructured electrical industry which is trying to improve efficiency at the minimum cost. The obvious economical solution is avoiding conventional development and utilizing distributed generation capability which provides nearby consumer with needed power. Using this category of power generators in the grid has various advantages as well as its problems. One of the problems, which is usually caused by distributed generation, is islanding phenomenon. In this study a novel approach is proposed to detect islanding phenomenon for small scaled generators. Experimental results prove its speed and precision in detection of islanding phenomenon. Here, grid will continue its operation by using load shedding. When islanding is detected, special control system designed for DG synchronization is exploited to reconnect DG after fault compensation.

articleTitle: Modeling and Evaluation of Small Rooftop Photovoltaic Effects on Reliability Indices of Distribution System Considering Customers Type
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: One of the impacts of distributed generation on power distribution system is changing level of network reliability. This paper examines the effects of increasing level of penetration of rooftop photovoltaic power stations on the reliability indices of the distribution network. The study was performed on part of the distribution network of Tehran. For a more realistic study, the assessment was carried out under different scenarios of the distribution of resources as well as different levels of penetration. Also, different types of customer was considered in this research. The results indicated that these resources have desirable effect by improving the reliability indices of the network.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Energy Storage System in a Hybrid Microgrid Considering Load Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, the optimal operation of the energy storage system in a hybrid microgrid with respect to load uncertainty is examined. An energy storage system such as a battery or other energy storage technologies used in hybrid microgrids with multiple distributed generations (DGs) is considered. Optimal utilization of the storage system is to select the optimum location, determine the optimum capacity and optimal charging and discharging planning. The optimal operation of the storage system used in the hybrid microgrid is challenging due to uncertainties in various system parameters. The optimization problem in this paper is a nonlinear and non-convex problem, therefore ordinary problem solving methods such as linear programming are inapplicable. On the other hand, uncertainty of load, weather conditions and energy storage system can have a significant impact on the problem of optimal operation of the storage system. Moreover, a new optimization algorithm named stochastic quasi-gradient method (SQGM) is utilized in order to optimize the nonlinear and non-convex objective function under load uncertainty. Simulation results on a typical hybrid microgrid confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of the 1.2 Megawatt Photovoltaic Power Plant with a Hybrid Concentrated Solar Power/Fossil Fuel system in Iran
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Greenhouse gas emission increased in recent years and it is the main reason for global warming. To overcome the challenges, sustainable and renewable energy sources are required. In this paper, an economic analysis fulfilled for 1.2-megawatt photovoltaic power plant with different tracking systems in several cities of Iran by RETScreen software. Moreover, results compared with the same capacity hybrid of concentrated solar power and fossil fuel power plant under several scenarios. The results show that the two-axis tracker photovoltaic power plant has 48% more capacity factor than a fixed state. Also, using the tracking system for the photovoltaic power plant and a thirty percent reduction in capital expenditure for the concentrated solar power system decreased the levelized cost of electricity by 21% and 28%, respectively. The minimum levelized cost of electricity is achieved US$ 0.084/kWh. Also, it was found that the concentrated solar power system reduces greenhouses gas emission two times more than the same capacity of photovoltaic. Finally, the concentrated solar power has a better economic, environmental and technical performance than the photovoltaic system in the future.

articleTitle: Implementation and simulation of the optimal water supply system by the Pvsyst software and ultrasonic sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In today's world due to the growing water crisis the need for a reliable water supply system is a necessary requirement for any agricultural area. In the past water has become a commodity for human consumption but in a new approach water is an economic commodity and is considered to be the most important human need and it is important to manage supply and demand in this sector and put it in parallel.. One of the important issues in management is the decision to use water systems and water distribution networks which if properly selected can improve the efficiency of consumption which is in the subset of that consumption pattern. The proposed system in this research attempts to provide a system with high safety and efficiency and fewer losses. In this project we tried to examine a solar water pump system simulated by the PVSYST software along with a surface measurement of ultrasonic waves which was programmed by an AVR processor.

articleTitle: Distribution Loss Reduction Using centralized feeders
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper looks into different methods of loss reduction in 20 kV distribution networks. Due to urban congestion, required boundaries, unsuitable locations and lack of enough 63/20 kV substations, network expansion and building new feeders are difficult and make some feeders overload and also the length of the feeders must be increased. Therefore, feeder losses increased considerably. This paper tries to deal with such difficulty by introducing centralized feeders. The feeders in addition to economic benefits and simple implementation, need no space and present high performance in this situation so can reduce network losses, significantly. The optimization of such feeders is investigated using the Lagrangian method, and the best feeding mode is used to reduce distribution losses, considerably. The simple and practical method can reduce network losses up to at least 47% while it is easy to implement and need minimum requirements. The method is implemented in 20 kV distribution system of Chalus city, Iran, where total losses of the network is reduced from %4 to %2.

articleTitle: A new design for Stirling engine with the high performance for using in urban solar CHP
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The Stirling engine Due to its structure has the potential for use in CHP systems. On the other hand, due to its external combustion chamber, the engine can use renewable energy sources such as solar and geothermal energy and etc. as the source of energy. But hitherto, due to the low efficiency of these engines, they were not economical to use. In this article, first tried to review the type of structure of the Stirling engines, then a variety of numerical modeling, the weaknesses, and advantages of the previous engines are argued, and finally introduce a new structure that called by this article the Delta type. The numerical modeling of this motor was done by MATLAB software. The results indicate that the electrical efficiency and total electrical and thermal efficiency of the engine are 49% and 95%, respectively, as compared to the previous types of Stirling engines 20% increased, and hopefully, in practice, will have better efficiency than previous ones.

articleTitle: Influence of the Substrate Porosity on the Electrical Performance of a Hybrid Silicon Photo Voltaic
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper describes a novel hybrid silicon photo voltaic structure with a tremendous three times enhancement in open circuit voltage and short circuit current. This is a considerable result in a photo voltaic device with 0.196 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> effective surface area and porous layer on the top surface of the p-type poly-silicon substrate. This substrate is covered with gold layers on both sides following by a titanium dioxide layer and an indium tin oxide layer on the top surface, respectively. An aluminum layer at the back surface completes this novel architecture. The technique of the creation of pores on the p-type substrate resulted in a significant enhancement in open circuit voltage from 17mV to 44 mV and short circuit current from 2.64 μA to 7.66 μA. The fill factor (FF) was also improved from 23% to 24%.

articleTitle: Investigation of an Appropriate Location for Construction the Large-Scale Photovoltaic Power Plant in Southeastern Iran
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper investigated a techno-economic evaluation of the one-axis tracker photovoltaic power plant with 10 megawatt capacity in southeast of Iran. The southeast region of Iran has a hot and dry climate and great potential of solar radiation. Reviewing solar radiation atlases and the average air temperature in this particular region, ten cities were selected as case studies. RETScreen software was used to calculate technical and economic parameters such as the cost of energy production, capacity factor, payback period, internal rate of return, net present value, benefit-cost ratio and gross reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. The results showed that using the one-axis tracker system increases the capacity factor of the power plant by approximate one-third relative to the fixed panel state. Moreover, the payback period of investment was achieved less than 4 years in all the studied cities. Considering all of the above parameters, we compared selected cities with each other from economical point of view. Finally, the results led to determine the best location for the large-scale photovoltaic power plant construction.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of Electric Vehicle Parking Lots for Minimizing Distribution System Costs Considering Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The spread of Electric Vehicles (EVs) increases the use of vehicles' batteries for grid support. To achieve the process of sustainable development, the integration of EVs in a scheduled procedure is essential. One of the critical solutions is the optimal allocation of Electric Vehicle Parking Lots (EVPLs). Therefore, this paper aims to allocate Parking Lots (PLs) in the distribution system, considering the uncertainty associated with the behavior of EVs' owners and the output power of PLs. PLs provide Vehicle- to-Grid (V2G) power in the distribution system as a new type of Distributed Generations (DGs). Minimizing the overall costs of the system, including power loss, system reliability, energy transported from the main grid, the net energy of charging/discharging the batteries of EVs and installation cost of PLs are considered as possible objectives. Finally, the proposed scheme in the methodology section is applied to the IEEE 33-bus distribution system by using the Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) and taking the power systems' prevailing constraints as well as the restrictions pertaining to EVs into consideration. The simulation results show a dramatic improvement in the system operating conditions.

articleTitle: Large utility scale PV power plant optimum site selection in Iran using GIS analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Iran is ranked 20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> in the world in terms of land area and also enjoys excellent solar irradiation throughout its land area. Although at first glance site selection for large utility scale PV power plant in Iran seems a trivial task only limited by closeness to electrical grid, roads, points of electrical consumption, site meteorological data, etc. further examination reveals that parameters such that slope of the site, direction of the slope, site altitude, large scale sand and dust storms, local sand and dust storms, etc. have a direct influence on the performance of the PV power plant as well as the CAPEX and OPEX of the power plant. This papers aims to emphasize the parameters that are usually ignored in the process of site selection of large utility scale PV power plants. For the purpose of this paper the capacity ≤ 100 MW (AC) in a single site is classified as small utility scale PV power plant and a PV power plant with capacity > 100 MW (AC) in a single site is classified as large utility scale PV power plant. Residential and commercial PV systems are not considered in the current paper irrespective of their installed capacities.

articleTitle: Optimal Management of Distributed Generations in a Residential Complex Using Cuckoo Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: this paper presents an optimal management of distributed generation energy resources in a residential complex as a microgrid. For this purpose, distributed generators such as, wind turbine, photovoltaic array, micro turbine, fuel cell and battery are used in the studied system. To manage these resources accurately, an objective function based on operation cost of microgrid and Cuckoo Search algorithm used, respectively. To run the simulation, required amount of energy of the complex over a 24-hour period is calculated. Results indicate that the presence of distributed generators and proper energy management have had considerable effects on reducing costs of energy.

articleTitle: Experimental investigating the effect of PCM on solar air heater with fin
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this study, a solar air heater with PCM storage system has been investigated in the Kashmar in the Razavi Khorasan Province of Iran. The ambient temperature, the output temperature were measured and the sun radiation was calculated. The measured temperatures were calculated on different flow rates. The performance of solar air heater was measured by the first Law of thermodynamics and energy efficiency. By comparing the results for all flow rates, it was found that, as the flow rate increases, the output temperature decreases, but the efficiency of the solar air heater increases. Also, by comparing the performance of current solar air heater with the numerical study (without a fin and without a power storage system) it was shown that the efficiency was enhanced with PCM and fin tangibly.

articleTitle: A Case Study of Energy Harvesting by Dynamic Tidal Power in the Persian Gulf
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Dynamic Tidal Power (DTP) is one of the most recent methods of exploiting the energy of tides. Although most of the studies regarding this revolutionary method aim at the Yellow and Bohai seas in China, the evaluation of this method in other potential locations in the world is of considerable importance. This study provides preliminary insights and assessments about the use of this method in Faror strait in the Persian Gulf. By using a 3D numerical model of a full-scale domain, the maximum water level difference between the two sides of the DTP dam is found to be about 1.2 meters at the maximum water speed in the strait with a total available power of 760 MW. Furthermore, among the existing technologies for electric generators, a direct-drive permanent magnet synchronous generator has proved to be the best choice for the electric power generation system. Moreover, it has been concluded that power electronic converters are required to make the generated voltage compatible with the grid voltage.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Solar Water Cooling System
publicationTitle: 2019 Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy & Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, ever-increasing depletion of energy resources and high electrical energy demand by conventional condensation systems have led researchers to search for energy-efficient systems. In this research, a solar water cooling system is designed and developed in a way to be highly effective in minimizing electrical energy consumption. The overall energy consumption by the obtained compression refrigeration system is 980 watts, which comprises of a compressor (887W), a fan (90 watts) and other consumables. To meet this power consumption, the electrical energy produced by solar panels in an area of about 6 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with 4 photovoltaic (PV) panels is approximately 1280 W. Another advantage of the system is the capability of connection to other devices such as various types of water desalination systems, obtaining much more water with a temperature lower than ambient temperatures. In the experimental results, it was observed that this system was able to cool 50 liters of water from a temperature of 28 °C down to 7 °C in less than 20 minutest.
